about.title: Biggs Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Biggs is a small city, but its roads still carry the same real risks any driver faces — sudden stops on SR-99, cross-traffic at 5th Street and E Street, or a distracted driver near Midway. When a collision happens here, the aftermath can feel overwhelming: medical appointments, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Because Butte County crash reports, photos, and witness statements can disappear or fade quickly, getting matched with someone who can start preserving that evidence early matters. Whether your crash happened on a Sunday afternoon or a quiet weekday morning, the goal is the same: get you connected with someone who can evaluate what happened and explain your options clearly, without pressure.
commonInjuries: Torn ligaments or soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims involving a government road or vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help make sure that deadline isn't missed.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Rules
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your compensation is reduced by your share of blame. How fault gets assigned matters, which is why a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney can work against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in car accident cases the way some states do. An attorney can help make sure those losses are properly accounted for, not just medical bills and lost wages.

items.question: I was in a crash near 5th Street in Biggs — do I really need a lawyer for a small-town accident?
items.answer: Even in a small city like Biggs, insurance companies handle claims the same way they would in a larger city, and they're not on your side. An independent attorney can help you understand what your claim may be worth and handle communications with the insurer. LawProactive's matching service is free, so there's no cost to at least find out where you stand.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney, since anything you say can be used to reduce or deny your claim later. Insurers often ask leading questions designed to establish fault or minimize injuries. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Biggs?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like a public road agency, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later. An attorney can confirm the exact deadline that applies to your situation.
